title: Vault credential-slot names are a three-file implicit contract; the authType parameter is decorative and disagrees with reality
existing_state: VaultService passes "token"/"approle"/"ldap"/"userpass" as the second argument to its credential providers (Services/Vault/VaultService.cs:317, 329, 370, 408, 884), but every production provider discards that argument: Form1's lambdas bind it to _ and hardcode the different literals "token"/"approle_secret"/"ldap_password"/"userpass_password" (Form1.cs:1396-1415), and SettingsDialog independently hardcodes the same four strings when persisting secrets (SettingsDialog.cs:1013-1016) and ignores the parameter again in its Test Connection providers (SettingsDialog.cs:1062-1066). The system works only because two UI files agree by copy-paste convention; any future caller that trusts the parameter VaultService actually sends (e.g. "approle") reads or writes a credential slot that nothing else uses. Compounding it, Token auth and the OIDC persisted-token fast path share the same ":token" slot (read at VaultService.cs:317 and :884, written by the tokenSaver at Form1.cs:1416-1420), so toggling a profile between Token and OIDC auth silently overwrites the user's static token with short-lived OIDC tokens.
recommendation: Promote the four authType literals to constants on CredentialTargets (already the declared single source of truth for target names in Services/Credentials/CredentialTargets.cs), make VaultService pass those constants, and change the Form1/SettingsDialog provider lambdas to use the parameter instead of ignoring it — deleting the duplicate literals. Give OIDC its own slot constant (e.g. "oidc_token") with a one-time fallback read of the legacy "token" slot so existing logins survive.
user_benefit: Eliminates a latent wrong-credential-slot trap that will bite the next feature touching Vault auth (the compiler will enforce the contract instead of copy-paste), and stops OIDC logins from clobbering a user's stored static Vault token.
